title: bug: archive_epic archives BLOCKED rows without clearing their blocked* fields, and report_blocked reads stored blockedOnTaskIds on non-BLOCKED rows, so a real block on an un-archived row answers dependenciesSatisfied and is never recorded
description:
Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveEpic.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reportBlocked.ts, and their tests archiveEpic.test.ts and reportBlocked.test.ts. The clearing code may be shared with archiveTask.ts. No open row declares any of these files. I checked the plan files of every non-DONE row at 2026-11-02 20:51Z.

Defect, read at HEAD 3e092cff:
- archive_epic's IN_FLIGHT list (archiveEpic.ts:11) leaves out BLOCKED, so BLOCKED rows are archived, and its loop writes a bare { status: 'ARCHIVED' } (:61-64).
- archive_task (archiveTask.ts:64-74) and set_task_status (setTaskStatus.ts:179-188) both copy the reason to priorBlockedReason and null blockedReason, blockedResourceId, blockedOnTaskIds, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt when a row leaves BLOCKED. updateTask itself clears none of them.
- Un-archiving (set_task_status ARCHIVED→BACKLOG/WORKING, setTaskStatus.ts:53) clears block fields only when the row is BLOCKED, so the stale ids ride along into WORKING. get_context and list_tasks show the fields only for BLOCKED rows, so nobody sees them.
- report_blocked reads the stored ids whatever the row's status (reportBlocked.ts:172) and computes dependenciesSatisfied from them (:256).
- Suppose a worker on the un-archived row reports a real non-task blocker with blockedOnTaskIds:[], and a stale id is DONE:
  - The answer is dependenciesSatisfied:true ("NOT blocked … Continue the task").
  - Nothing is written and nobody is paged, and every retry gives the same answer.
- If the stale id is not DONE, the row blocks on it instead of on the real blocker, and auto-unblocks when it lands.
- Second source, same effect: release_task's refusal cascade parks a BLOCKED, assigned row to BACKLOG with no clearing (releaseTask.ts:326-327). Clearing there is out of scope here; the report_blocked guard below removes its effect on report_blocked.
- The stale ids also feed dependencyEdges (cycle checks) and get_context's declared prerequisites.

Reach: archive_epic on an epic that holds a BLOCKED row with ids, followed by any un-archive; or the refusal cascade on such a row. The trigger is rare, but the outcome is a worker that cannot park its task.

Origin: hunt requested by governor-e6b40560 (msg-5fe3b1537cb04b50964bd0edf07db4c8). No existing row mentions archive_epic together with blocked fields. docs/MCP_SERVER.md already says blocked* fields belong to BLOCKED tasks only, so no doc edit is needed.
definitionOfDone: archive_epic clears a BLOCKED row's block fields exactly as archive_task does: priorBlockedReason keeps the reason, and blockedReason, blockedResourceId, blockedOnTaskIds, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt become null. Non-BLOCKED rows are archived as before, and the in-flight refusal and finalizing-attempt gate are unchanged.

report_blocked merges stored blockedOnTaskIds only when the row is already BLOCKED (the union-on-update arm). On a PLANNING, WORKING or REVIEW row that carries stale ids, the block is computed from the supplied or reason-parsed ids alone. With blockedOnTaskIds:[], the row is parked BLOCKED with no ids and paged as a dep-less block.

New cases: archiveEpic.test.ts archives a BLOCKED row and asserts every cleared field. reportBlocked.test.ts blocks a WORKING row carrying a stale DONE blockedOnTaskIds entry with blockedOnTaskIds:[] and asserts blocked:true, status BLOCKED and no stored ids. RED first against the unchanged code, with the failing output quoted. Existing cases in both files pass unchanged.

`cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/archiveEpic.test.ts src/tools/reportBlocked.test.ts src/tools/archiveTask.test.ts src/tools/setTaskStatus.test.ts` exits 0. Run it in the task's worktree or in a git-archive snapshot, never as an in-place build or test in the shared control checkout. Its output is the complete_task evidence.
No docs/ edit. Only archiveEpic.ts, reportBlocked.ts and their two test files change, plus archiveTask.ts if the clearing code is extracted into a shared helper (its behaviour unchanged).

- Archive epic-1 and expect archivedTaskCount 2.
- task-bk toMatchObject { status: 'ARCHIVED', priorBlockedReason: 'needs PostgreSQL', blockedReason: null, blockedResourceId: null, blockedOnTaskIds: null, blockedFromStatus: null, blockedAt: null }.
- task-done is ARCHIVED and (priorBlockedReason ?? null) is null: non-BLOCKED rows archive as before.
- set_task_status task-bk ARCHIVED→WORKING, then expect { status: 'WORKING', blockedOnTaskIds: null, blockedFromStatus: null }.
Every block field starts non-null, so each assertion can fail. The prerequisite sits in ANOTHER epic on purpose: updateTask runs runDependencyUnblock on every DONE/ARCHIVED transition, so a prerequisite archived by the same call could restore task-bk mid-loop, depending on readdir order (flaky across platforms). blockedResourceId also keeps that scan off the row.

(b) reportBlocked.test.ts, first describe, just before the it.each 'drops dependency cycles and alerts #governors (explicit=%s)':
- Case A 'a WORKING row carrying a stale DONE blockedOnTaskIds entry blocks on [] alone: parked dep-less, stale ids cleared'. Setup: const stale = await state.createTask({ epicId: 'epic-1', title: 'Old prerequisite', status: 'DONE' }); then state.tasks.set('task-1', { ...state.getTask('task-1')!, blockedOnTaskIds: [stale.id] }), a fixture write like the one in 'auto-unblocks on the real dependency…'. Call: result = await report({ reason: 'staging DB is down', blockedOnTaskIds: [] }). Expect:
  - result.blocked not.toBe(false); result.dependenciesSatisfied undefined; result.taskStatus 'BLOCKED';
  - result.blockedOnTaskIds and result.satisfiedBlockedOnTaskIds undefined; result.seatFreed true;
  - result.blockResolution toContain 'No unmet blockedOnTaskIds were recorded';
  - result.notified toEqual { target: '@governors', via: 'governors-fallback' } (the fixture has no architect), and one mentionedGeneralPosts() entry contains 'blocked on task-1' and the reason;
  - stored task-1 has status 'BLOCKED' and (blockedOnTaskIds ?? null) null;
  - await runDependencyUnblock(state) returns [] and task-1 stays BLOCKED.
- Case B 'a stale OPEN id on a WORKING row is not unioned into an explicit list: the row waits on the real blocker only'. Setup: stale and real are both WORKING; fixture task-1 blockedOnTaskIds [stale.id]. Call: report({ reason: `waiting on ${real.id}`, blockedOnTaskIds: [real.id] }). Expect result.blockedOnTaskIds and the stored ids toEqual [real.id]. Fixture stale → DONE: runDependencyUnblock returns []. Fixture real → DONE: it returns ['task-1'].

DoD 3's 'asserts blocked:true' is read as pinned by TASK rail proposal prop-583816507c344cfeaa139033c7c6193c (approved or pending). The Blocked answer has no `blocked` key, so case A asserts blocked is not false, dependenciesSatisfied undefined and taskStatus 'BLOCKED'. Do not add a `blocked` response field.

- archiveEpic: expected { id: 'task-bk', …(25) } to match object { status: 'ARCHIVED', …(6) };

implementationPlan.description:
archive_epic clears block fields through one helper shared with archive_task (DoD 1, DoD 5).

archiveTask.ts: move the existing clear-on-exit block (archiveTask.ts:64-74) verbatim into an exported pure function above archiveTaskTool:
  export function archiveUpdates(task: Pick<Task, 'status' | 'blockedReason'>): Partial<Task>
It returns { status: 'ARCHIVED' }. When task.status === 'BLOCKED' it also sets priorBlockedReason = task.blockedReason (only when truthy) and sets blockedReason, blockedResourceId, blockedOnTaskIds, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt to null. Keep the 'same clear-on-exit as set_task_status' comment on the helper. archive_task's handler then calls state.updateTask(task.id, archiveUpdates(task), 'TASK_ARCHIVED'). ARCHIVABLE_FROM, HOLDER_ONLY_FROM, the holder check and the idempotent return are untouched, so archiveTask.test.ts passes unchanged.

archiveEpic.ts: import { archiveUpdates } from './archiveTask.js' and replace the loop's bare { status: 'ARCHIVED' } (archiveEpic.ts:63) with archiveUpdates(task). These stay byte-identical: IN_FLIGHT, the refusal message, the assertNoFinalizingAttempt pre-pass, the epic update, the tool description and the return shape. Only the IN_FLIGHT doc comment may add that a BLOCKED row is shelveable with its block fields cleared.

Keep the loop on the pre-loop snapshot `task`. If an earlier sibling's ARCHIVED transition auto-unblocks a BLOCKED row mid-loop, the snapshot still reads BLOCKED, so the row still ends ARCHIVED with null block fields. That mid-loop restore is pre-existing and out of scope.

Error handling: the helper is pure (no IO, cannot throw). updateTask failures propagate exactly as today, and the all-or-nothing gates still run before the first write.
implementationPlan.note: Extracted archive_task's clearing unchanged into pure typed archiveUpdates and reused it in archive_epic. All gates, permissions, idempotency, events and response shapes untouched. Regression case proved RED in step 1; GREEN gate batched at approved step 4. Noticed snapshot-recipe amendment from completion response and re-read effective context before further verification.

Guarded stored dependency IDs by current post-await BLOCKED status; fresh flips now always write recorded IDs or null, clearing stale IDs on both resource and non-resource paths. Updated only dependency comment, guard and flip write. Already-BLOCKED union, validation, cycles, satisfied filtering, paging, seats and API shape unchanged. Existing collection logic reused; step-1 RED reproduced both defects; GREEN verification is next.

implementationPlan.description:

(a) Parity: archive_epic and archive_task now write the same clearing through one helper. set_task_status's BLOCKED exit (setTaskStatus.ts:179-188) clears the same five fields and sets priorBlockedReason.
(b) The already-BLOCKED repeat arm still unions stored ids, satisfied ones included: 'a repeat carrying NEW blockedOnTaskIds…' and 'the reason-update arm on an already-BLOCKED row KEEPS satisfied ids…' pass unchanged.
(c) A fresh flip never leaves an earlier list: it writes the recorded ids, otherwise null, on resource and non-resource flips alike.
(d) Concurrency: both tools run under the global state mutex, and the new guard reads the post-await task.
(e) blockedOnTaskIds that is null, undefined, [] or not an array gives stored [] on every status.
(f) Mutation check in a scratch copy of the snapshot, never in the worktree. Revert each runtime hunk on its own and confirm a new case fails:
  - the status guard → cases A and B;
  - the null write → case A's stored-ids assertion;
  - archiveUpdates in archive_epic → the archiveEpic case.
  Then confirm the restored copy passes.
(g) Put residuals in the handoff, not in code. release_task's refusal cascade and set_task_status's un-archive still leave block fields on a non-BLOCKED row. Those stale ids still feed dependencyEdges/findDependencyPath (a false DEPENDENCY_CYCLE drop) and get_context's declared prerequisites.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Add `blocked: true` to report_blocked's Blocked response so DoD 3 can assert it literally. Rejected: it changes the documented response contract (docs/MCP_SERVER.md Returns) and DoD 5 forbids the docs edit. The reading is pinned by TASK rail prop-583816507c344cfeaa139033c7c6193c instead. 2) Copy the 7-line clearing into archiveEpic.ts. Rejected in favour of one helper in archiveTask.ts, so 'exactly as archive_task does' holds by construction (DoD 5 allows it). 3) Add BLOCKED to archive_epic's IN_FLIGHT list. Rejected: DoD 1 keeps the refusal unchanged, and archive_task already shelves BLOCKED rows. 4) Clear fields on un-archive (setTaskStatus.ts:53) or in release_task's refusal cascade. Both files are outside DoD 5's list; the report_blocked guard removes their effect on report_blocked. 5) Write null only when stale ids exist. Rejected for the unconditional write, which mirrors blockedResourceId; the architect's scratch run found no regression. 6) Re-read the live row inside archive_epic's loop: not needed, because the snapshot still reads BLOCKED and the clearing is still right.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: updateTask clears no blocked* field; only set_task_status, archive_task and runDependencyUnblock do. updateTask runs runDependencyUnblock on every DONE/ARCHIVED transition (taskStore.ts:670-681), and that scan skips rows with blockedResourceId. get_context and list_tasks show blocked* only on BLOCKED rows, so stale ids stay invisible. report_blocked refuses human-gated rows before line 171, so there `!flipped` means BLOCKED. Test idiom for absent-or-null: `(x ?? null)` toBeNull. ToolTestHarness.createEpic/createTask write JSON fixtures; call h.state.load() after them. The reportBlocked fixture has worker-1 (role worker) and no architect, so pages fall back to @governors.
planningNotes.risks: (1) A snapshot from `git archive HEAD` without the worktree overlay tests the unchanged code and gives a false green; the step-1 recipe overlays `git diff --name-only HEAD`. (2) A same-epic prerequisite in the archiveEpic fixture is order-dependent through the event-driven unblock, so use the cross-epic dependency. (3) The flip now writes `"blockedOnTaskIds": null` into fresh BLOCKED rows without ids. Plugins already read null there (runDependencyUnblock writes it). (4) Peer row task-1cb3f280 (PLANNING) edits dependencyUnblock.ts and runs reportBlocked.test.ts without editing it. There is no file overlap, and worktree mode isolates RED tests. (5) Rail proposal prop-58381650 may still be pending at QA; cite it in complete_task.
